Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

1) What we heard
- Primary goal: reduce per-1M token inference spend for your customer-facing chat product while keeping P95 latency under 400ms.
- You're running mostly 8k-context models today via Hyperscaler API with ~60% cacheable prefixes (welcome message, system prompts, product FAQs).

2) Redwood differentiators to validate in tests
- Lower per-token unit cost driven by batching + KV prefix caching and quantization-friendly execution.
- Predictable latency via reserved pools or regional routing (avoids noisy neighbor issues).
- Transparent unit economics: we can break down per-1M tokens across tokenization, batching efficiency, cache hit assumptions.

3) Proposed quick tests (2-week):
- Benchmark parity test: 50k sample requests replayed vs your current Hyperscaler endpoint and Redwood hosted endpoint (same model family). Measure cost/1M tokens, median/P95 latency, and throughput.
- Cache/batch sensitivity: run with simulated cache-hit rates at 40/60/80% and batching windows of 20/50/100ms to surface cost delta.
- Edge case: long context 6–8k runs to validate KV cache behavior and memory pressure.

4) Ask from your side
- Share 50k anonymized request samples (headers redacted) and a representative token distribution (short/medium/long).
- Confirm target SLA: P95 <= 400ms? or is 300ms the true requirement?

I've attached a quick pricing spreadsheet that models per-1M token cost under different batching and cache scenarios (redwood-pricing-1Mtokens.xlsx) plus our TCO assumptions (redwood-tco-assumptions.pdf).

Next step: If this sounds good, can we schedule the 2-hour replay window Tuesday or Wednesday next week?

Great questions — below is a concise summary you can share with folks internally. I also attached a one-page breakdown in the TCO assumptions PDF.

Assumptions behind the per-1M token line in spreadsheet:
- Model: open-weights equivalent to MPT-7B-style performance (you can swap in your exact model).
- Token mix: based on your histogram — avg length 28 tokens, 60% short (<32 tokens), 30% medium (32–256), 10% long (>256).
- Batching: continuous batching with batching window 50ms yields batching factor ~6x for your traffic profile. We show three windows (20/50/100ms).
- Cache/KV hit rate: we model 40/60/80% scenarios. Cacheable prefixes (system + conversation context) materially reduce per-request compute.
- Overhead: include KV priming cost on first cold request (amortized across sessions) and a small model warm-up multiplier (5% of token cost) for short-lived sessions.

Example numbers (high-level, back-of-envelope) — per 1M tokens served to your public chat users: 
- Hyperscaler X (current): $48.5 / 1M tokens (measured from your billing + our calibration)
- Redwood hosted (no reserved capacity): $32–36 / 1M tokens depending on batching window and cache hit rate
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity, 1yr): $22–28 / 1M tokens for sustained throughput and higher batching efficiency

Where the savings come from:
- Batching multiplier: >3x improvement in device utilization vs naive 1-request-per-call patterns common on hyperscaler APIs.
- KV/prefix cache: when hit rates are 60%+, effective compute executed per user request drops significantly (we modeled this explicitly).
- Quantization & kernel selection: compute-efficient runtime kernels reduce GPU cycles per token.

Notes & caveats:
- If your traffic is extremely spiky with low concurrency, batching benefits will be lower. That’s where reserved capacity (Dedicated) helps guarantee concurrency to enable batching.
- Long-context workloads increase memory pressure and may reduce batching efficiency; we’ll measure this in the replay.

Suggested next tests:
- We can run a 50k replay this week. I recommend 3 runs: (A) baseline Hyperscaler X replay, (B) Redwood hosted, (C) Redwood Dedicated (if you want reserved pool numbers). Each run will produce: cost/1M tokens, median/P95 latency, batching factor, observed cache hit rate.

I’ll schedule the replay once you confirm the window. If you want, I can also include a sample breakdown email comparing exact per-token components (compute, memory, infra) for your CFO.

Best,
